proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(m_\ell=(a_{0\ell},A_{\ell\cdot})^\prime\). Under \(\mathsf P_n(\theta)\), the pre-block observations have mean \(m_\ell\), the observed post-donor observations have mean \(d\), and the contemporaneous pre covariance is \(\Sigma\). Hence the observed law determines \(A,a_0,d,\Sigma\), and therefore \(z(\theta)\). Conversely, the factorization and error-law coordinates in \(\theta\in\Theta_n\), together with Definition \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}map}\), satisfy every member property of \(\mathcal M_n\), so \(\mathsf P_n(\theta)\in\mathcal M_n\). If \(P\in\mathcal M_n\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:block\mbox{-}factor\mbox{-}means}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:stationary\mbox{-}errors}\) supply \(A,a_0,d,\Sigma\) and \(\mathsf Q_\varepsilon\); the remaining member conditions put the tuple in \(\Theta_n\), and its pushforward is \(P\). Thus the map is onto, though \(\mathsf Q_\varepsilon\) need not be identified beyond observed cylinders.

For a cylinder event \(B\), \(P_\theta(B)\) is a finite-dimensional cylinder probability of \(\mathsf Q_\varepsilon\) after a Euclidean translation by signal coordinates. It is measurable in the product sigma-field of Definition \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}law\mbox{-}map}\). A monotone-class argument starting from cylinders proves measurability of \(\theta\mapsto P_\theta\) for the evaluation sigma-field.

Finally, \(X=SA\) and \(x=Sa_0\), so the program defining \(w_{P_\theta}(v)\) depends only on \(A,a_0\). Its Hessian is at least \(2\rho I_J\), hence its minimizer is unique. The formula for \(R_{P_\theta}\) then depends only on \(A,a_0,d,\Sigma\). Consequently all representations of the same observed law agree on \(z(\theta)\), \(w_{P_\theta}\), and \(R_{P_\theta}\).

Write \(A=F_{\mathrm{pre}}U_D\). By Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:rank\mbox{-}spectrum}\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\). Since \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}\) has \(r\) columns and \(U_D\) has \(r\) rows,
\[
r=\operatorname{rank}(F_{\mathrm{pre}}U_D)\leq\min\{\operatorname{rank}(F_{\mathrm{pre}}),\operatorname{rank}(U_D)\}\leq r,
\]
so \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}\) has full column rank and \(U_D\) has full row rank. If \(A\gamma=a_0\), Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:block\mbox{-}factor\mbox{-}means}\) gives
\[
F_{\mathrm{pre}}(U_D\gamma-\mu_0)=A\gamma-a_0=0.
\]
Thus \(U_D\gamma=\mu_0\), and since \(d^\prime=f_{\mathrm{post}}^\prime U_D\),
\[
d^\prime\gamma=f_{\mathrm{post}}^\prime U_D\gamma=f_{\mathrm{post}}^\prime\mu_0,
\]
the target untreated post mean. Moreover \(a_0\in\operatorname{col}(A)\), so \(AA^+a_0=a_0\), and \(\gamma=A^+a_0\) is one solution. Hence \(c_0=d^\prime A^+a_0\). If \(\widetilde\gamma\) is another solution, then \(U_D(\widetilde\gamma-\gamma)=0\) and \(d^\prime(\widetilde\gamma-\gamma)=0\). Under any invertible factor rotation \(G\), the factors change to \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}G\) and \(G^{-1}U_D\), while \(A,a_0,d\) and \(d^\prime A^+a_0\) do not change. This proves identification and both invariances.

Apart from a constant independent of \(w\), the criterion equals
\[
\frac12w^\prime H(v)w-f(v)^\prime w,\qquad H(v)=2\{X^\prime\operatorname{diag}(v)X+\rho I_J\}.
\]
Since \(H(v)\succeq2\rho I_J\), there is one minimizer. With equality multiplier \(\eta\) and slack \(s\), the necessary and sufficient KKT equations are
\[
H(v)w-f(v)+\eta\mathbf1-s=0,\quad \mathbf1^\prime w=1,\quad w\geq0,\quad s\geq0,\quad w_js_j=0.
\]
Fix \(B=\{j:w_j>0\}\neq\varnothing\). Complementarity gives \(s_B=0\), whence
\[
w_B=H_{BB}^{-1}(f_B-\eta\mathbf1),\qquad
\eta=\frac{\mathbf1^\prime H_{BB}^{-1}f_B-1}{\mathbf1^\prime H_{BB}^{-1}\mathbf1}.
\]
The inverse exists and the denominator is positive because \(H_{BB}\succeq2\rho I\). On \(B^c\),
\[
s_{B^c}=H_{B^cB}w_B-f_{B^c}+\eta\mathbf1.
\]
Thus the candidate satisfies all KKT equations exactly when \(w_B>0\) and \(s_{B^c}\geq0\). Sufficiency also follows directly: for every feasible \(\widetilde w\),
\[
\{H(v)w-f(v)\}^\prime(\widetilde w-w)=(-\eta\mathbf1+s)^\prime(\widetilde w-w)=s^\prime\widetilde w\geq0.
\]

The entries of \(H,f\) are affine polynomials in \(v\). By the adjugate formula, \(H_{BB}^{-1},w_B,\eta_B,s_{B^c}\) are rational with denominators strictly positive on \(\Delta_K\). Clearing them turns all sign restrictions into polynomial inequalities. Refining each support region by zero/strict inactive-slack signs gives finitely many semialgebraic strata covering \(\Delta_K\). On each stratum \(w_P(v)\) is rational. On the fixed-rank signal set, \(A^+\) is rational on each nonvanishing \(r\)-minor chart. Substitution into \(R_P\) makes \(G_P\) a finite union of semialgebraic graphs. Its coefficients \(A,a_0,d,\Sigma\) are the observed pre and donor-post means and the observed pre covariance, proving observability.

Let \(\bar\varepsilon_\ell=n_\ell^{-1}\sum_{t\in\ell}\varepsilon_t\) and \(q_t=\operatorname{vech}(\varepsilon_t\varepsilon_t^\prime-\Sigma)\). The mean expansions are exact:
\[
\sqrt n(\overline Y_\ell-m_\ell)=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_\ell}\sum_{t\in\ell}\varepsilon_t,\qquad
\sqrt n(\widehat d-d)=\frac{\sqrt n}{T_1}\sum_{t=n+1}^{n+T_1}\varepsilon_{D,t}.
\]
Block demeaning gives
\[
\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n(\varepsilon_t\varepsilon_t^\prime-\Sigma)
-\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac{n_\ell}{n}\bar\varepsilon_\ell\bar\varepsilon_\ell^\prime.
\]
Geometric absolute regularity and the sub-Gaussian bound imply, by truncation and the covariance decomposition for events \(k\) dates apart, that every coordinate product \(U_t\) of degree at most four satisfies \(|\operatorname{Cov}(U_0,U_k)|\leq Ce^{-ck}\) uniformly. Hence \(\sup_P\mathbb E_P\|\sqrt{n_\ell}\bar\varepsilon_\ell\|^2<\infty\), and, since \(L\) is fixed and \(n_\ell/n\) is bounded away from zero,
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{\ell=1}^L\frac{n_\ell}{n}\bar\varepsilon_\ell\bar\varepsilon_\ell^\prime=o_P(1)
\]
uniformly. Thus the covariance estimator has first-order term \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{t=1}^nq_t\), jointly with all mean terms.

For the uniform central limit step, apply any fixed unit vector to the weighted sums of \(\phi_t\). Divide each contiguous block into big blocks of length \(b_n=\lfloor n^{1/3}\rfloor\), separated by gaps \(g_n=\lceil C_0\log n\rceil\). The omitted-gap variance is \(O(g_n/b_n)\), and the absolute-regularity coupling error is \(O((n/b_n)e^{-cg_n})=o(1)\) for large \(C_0\). Coupled big-block sums are independent. Uniform moments imply Lindeberg because \(b_n/n\to0\), and characteristic-function expansion gives
\[
\prod_b\mathbb E\exp\{isS_{b,n}/\sqrt n\}
=\exp\{-s^2a^\prime V(P)a/2+o(1)\}
\]
uniformly for bounded \(s\) and \(P\). Restoring gaps and coupling, then applying all linear combinations, proves the uniform multivariate Gaussian approximation. Cross-covariances of distinct contiguous blocks are \(O(1)\) before normalization because \(\sum_{k\geq0}ke^{-ck}<\infty\), so they vanish. The limiting covariance has pre-mean blocks \(\Omega_{\varepsilon\varepsilon}/p_\ell\), mean--second-moment blocks \(\Omega_{\varepsilon q}\), second-moment block \(\Omega_{qq}\), and post-donor block \(\Omega_{\varepsilon_D\varepsilon_D}/\lambda\). The last is a long-run covariance, not \(\Sigma_{DD}/\lambda\), unless errors are serially independent.

If \(a_\ell,b,c\) multiply the pre means, covariance moment, and post mean, the limiting quadratic form is
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^Lp_\ell\,(a_\ell/p_\ell,b)^\prime\Omega(a_\ell/p_\ell,b)
+\lambda^{-1}c^\prime\Omega_{\varepsilon_D\varepsilon_D}c.
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:sampling\mbox{-}fractions}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:long\mbox{-}run\mbox{-}spectrum}\) bound it above and away from zero for every nonzero coefficient vector.

For HAC consistency, take bandwidth \(b_n=C_1\log n\) and delete pairs crossing the \(L-1\) block boundaries. The covariance tail is \(O(e^{-cb_n})\); expanding covariance sums gives stochastic error \(O_P(b_n/\sqrt n)\); replacing \(\phi_t\) by \(\widehat\phi_t\) contributes \(O_P(b_n/\sqrt n+b_n^2/n)\); and the \(O(Lb_n^2)\) deleted pairs contribute \(O_P(b_n^2/n)\). All vanish uniformly. Thus \(\widehat V-V(P)\to_P0\) uniformly, completing the joint expansion and nonsingularity proof.

This proof uses the corrected empty-set convention proposed for Definition \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}band}\). By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:joint\mbox{-}moment\mbox{-}expansion}\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M_n\),
\[
\widehat V^{-1/2}\sqrt n\{\widehat z-z(\theta_P)\}\Longrightarrow N(0,I_{q_z}),
\]
where \(\theta_P\) represents \(P\). Hence
\[
\liminf_n\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_n}\Pr_P\{\theta_P\in E_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
On that event, simultaneously for every \(v\in\Delta_K\), \(R_P(v)=R_{P_{\theta_P}}(v)\in C_n(v)\).

For diameter, the fixed-rank spectral bound gives \(\|\widetilde A^+-A^+\|\leq C\|\widetilde A-A\|\) for close legal signals. Adding the two optimizer variational inequalities gives
\[
2\rho\|\widetilde w(v)-w(v)\|^2
\leq\langle\{H(v)-\widetilde H(v)\}w(v)+\widetilde f(v)-f(v),\widetilde w(v)-w(v)\rangle.
\]
Since \(\|w(v)\|\leq1\), \(S\) is bounded, and \(v\in\Delta_K\),
\[
\sup_{v\in\Delta_K}\|\widetilde w(v)-w(v)\|\leq C\|\widetilde z-z\|,
\qquad
\sup_{v\in\Delta_K}|R_{\widetilde\theta}(v)-R_\theta(v)|\leq C_R\|\widetilde z-z\|.
\]
No strict complementarity is used.

When \(\widehat V\) has eigenvalues in a fixed compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\), every two elements of nonempty \(E_n\) satisfy \(\|z(\theta)-z(\widetilde\theta)\|\leq C/\sqrt n\). Therefore
\[
\sup_{v\in\Delta_K}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}C_n(v)\leq C.
\]
Uniform consistency of \(\widehat V\) makes the complementary event vanish uniformly. If \(E_n=\varnothing\), the corrected interval has diameter zero. The feasible signal set is a finite union of bounded closed rank charts and the criterion is continuous on each chart, so finite-chart measurable minimization gives measurable endpoints. This proves coverage, measurability, and the stochastic diameter statement. On the same simultaneous event, \(R_P(\widehat v)\in C_n(\widehat v)\) for every measurable \(\widehat v\); uniformity includes selectors within \(O(n^{-1/2})\) of face changes.

Put \(\epsilon=n^{-1/2}\), \(H_{n,u,t}=H_{\theta_n(u)}(v_n(t))\), and define \(f_{n,u,t}\) analogously. Twice continuous differentiability in the local chart, compactness, and legality of \(v_n(t)\) uniformly for large \(n\) give
\[
H_{n,u,t}=H_0+\epsilon\dot H(u,t)+O(\epsilon^2),\qquad
f_{n,u,t}=f_0+\epsilon\dot f(u,t)+O(\epsilon^2).
\]
The ridge variational inequality first gives \(\sup_{u,t}\|w_{n,u,t}-w_0\|=O(\epsilon)\). A coordinate with \(w_{0j}>0\) remains positive. If \(w_{0j}=0<s_{0j}\), continuity of the multiplier keeps its slack positive, so complementarity makes \(w_{n,u,t,j}=0\). Remaining zero coordinates have \(s_{0j}=0\) and retain nonnegativity. Thus, for \(w=w_0+\epsilon k\), bounded feasible \(k\)'s reduce to \(\mathcal C_0\).

Subtract the objective at \(w_0\), divide by \(\epsilon^2\), and use \(H_0w_0-f_0=-\eta_0\mathbf1+s_0\). Equality makes the multiplier term vanish and positive-slack coordinates are fixed at zero. Uniformly on bounded \(k,u,t\), the criterion is
\[
\frac12k^\prime H_0k+Q(u,t)^\prime k+O(\epsilon)(1+\|k\|^2).
\]
Both it and its limit are \(2\rho\)-strongly convex. Subtracting variational inequalities shows their minimizers differ by \(O(\epsilon)\), uniformly. Hence
\[
w_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))=w_0+\epsilon h(u,t)+O(\epsilon^2).
\]
This includes any number of weak zero weights.

Let \(\gamma_0=A_0^+a_{0,0}\). Differentiating \(A\gamma=a_0\) gives \(A_0\dot\gamma=\dot a_0-\dot A\gamma_0\). Since \(d_0\in\operatorname{row}(A_0)\),
\[
\dot c(u)=\dot d(u)^\prime\gamma_0+d_0^\prime A_0^+\{\dot a_0(u)-\dot A(u)\gamma_0\}.
\]
Taylor expansion of risk gives, uniformly,
\[
\begin{split}
\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}
&=2b_0\{\dot c(u)-\dot d(u)^\prime w_0\}+e_0^\prime\dot\Sigma(u)e_0\\
&\quad+\{-2b_0d_0-2\Sigma_{D0}+2\Sigma_{DD}w_0\}^\prime h(u,t)+o(1)\\
&=a(u)+g^\prime h(u,t)+o(1).
\end{split}
\]
This displays all completion, donor-mean, covariance, and weight terms.

The cone \(\mathcal C_0\) is polyhedral, \(H_0\) is fixed positive definite, and \(Q\) is linear. Enumerating binding weak inequalities gives finitely many linear formulas with polyhedral feasibility regions. Uniqueness makes them agree on common boundaries, so \(h\) and \(\Psi_{\theta_0}\) are continuous piecewise affine. The variational inequality also gives
\[
\|h(u,t)-h(u',t')\|\leq(2\rho)^{-1}\|Q(u,t)-Q(u',t')\|,
\]
proving uniform continuity.

Fix finite \(F\subset\mathcal U\). For realized band \(C\), define
\[
A_F(C)=\{u\in F:\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\in C(t)\text{ for every }t\in\mathcal D\}.
\]
It is measurable by the simultaneous coverage convention. If \(u,u'\in A_F(C)\), both values lie in \(C(t)\), so \(d_\Psi(u,u')\leq\sup_t\operatorname{diam}C(t)\). Taking the finite maximum proves the first assertion and preserves each grid coverage event.

Conversely, for selected nonempty \(A\subseteq F\), set
\[
C_A(t)=\left[\min_{u\in A}\Psi(u,t),\max_{u\in A}\Psi(u,t)\right].
\]
Finite extrema are measurable, all selected curves are covered, and
\[
\sup_t\operatorname{diam}C_A(t)
=\sup_t\max_{u,u'\in A}|\Psi(u,t)-\Psi(u',t)|
=\max_{u,u'\in A}d_\Psi(u,u').
\]
For \(A=\varnothing\), use a fixed singleton outside the bounded family range. If \(F\) is a \(\delta\)-net and \(|\Psi(u,t)-\Psi(u_i,t)|\leq K_u\delta\), padding by \(K_u\delta\) covers \(u\) whenever its nearest \(u_i\) is selected and adds at most \(2K_u\delta\) to width. This is the needed finite reduction and avoids the false assertion that a continuum envelope accepts exactly the original continuum of curves.

For computation, enumerate the finitely many critical-cone cells for \(u,u'\). On each intersected cell pair, the curve difference is affine in \(t\), and cell restrictions are linear. Intersect with the linear restrictions defining \(\mathcal D\) and \(\|t\|_2\leq L_0\). Maximizing both signs of the affine difference is an SOCP. Closed cells are valid because formulas agree on boundaries. The finite maximum is \(d_\Psi(u,u')\).

Write \(I=I(\theta_0)\), \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}=1-\alpha\), and \(P_u=N(u,I^{-1})\). The local variational inequality gives finite \(K_u\) with \(\sup_t|\Psi(u,t)-\Psi(u',t)|\leq K_u\|u-u'\|\), hence \(D_\star\leq2K_uM<\infty\).

Equal-covariance Gaussian integration in the likelihood-ratio direction gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_u,P_{u_i})=2\Phi\!\left(\frac{\|I^{1/2}(u-u_i)\|}{2}\right)-1
\leq\frac{\|I^{1/2}\|\delta}{\sqrt{2\pi}}=:\bar\epsilon_\delta.
\]
Thus \(\epsilon_\delta\leq\bar\epsilon_\delta\). Quantize \(Z\) into cells \(o\in\mathcal O_h\). On each bounded cell reconstruct from \(P_0(\,\cdot\mid o)\), independently of \(u\). Since
\[
\log\frac{dP_u}{dP_0}(z)=u^\prime Iz-\frac12u^\prime Iu,
\]
its oscillation in a cell of diameter \(h\) is at most \(\|I\|Mh\), so conditional total variation is at most \(e^{\|I\|Mh}-1\). Use any fixed reconstruction on the tail cell. For \(R>M\),
\[
\tau_R:=\sup_{\|u\|\leq M}P_u\{Z\notin[-R,R]^q\}
\leq2q\exp\!\left[-\frac{(R-M)^2}{2\lambda_{\max}(I^{-1})}\right].
\]
Thus one computable deficiency is
\[
\epsilon_h=\min\{1,e^{\|I\|Mh}-1+\tau_R\},
\]
which tends to zero under the asserted limits.

Take any full-observation admissible band and record the accepted subset of \(\mathcal U_N\) as in Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:curve\mbox{-}decision\mbox{-}reduction}\). Its subset cost is bounded by the band loss, and every grid inclusion probability is at least \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}\). Passing this rule through the reconstruction kernel makes it cell-measurable, lowers coverage by at most \(\epsilon_h\), and changes expected bounded cost by at most \(D_\star\epsilon_h\). Therefore
\[
V_{N,h}(q_{\mathrm{cov}}-\epsilon_h)-D_\star\epsilon_h\leq L_\alpha.
\]
This applies to arbitrary randomized measurable bands.

Conversely, take a feasible finite rule at level \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}+\epsilon_\delta\). If it selects \(A\neq\varnothing\), output
\[
\left[\min_{i\in A}\Psi(u_i,t)-K_u\delta,\ \max_{i\in A}\Psi(u_i,t)+K_u\delta\right],
\]
and use a fixed singleton for \(A=\varnothing\). For \(u\), choose \(u_i\) within \(\delta\). Inclusion of \(i\) covers the \(u\)-curve after padding. Total variation loses at most \(\epsilon_\delta\) coverage and changes expected unpadded cost by at most \(D_\star\epsilon_\delta\); padding adds \(2K_u\delta\). Hence
\[
L_\alpha\leq V_{N,h}(q_{\mathrm{cov}}+\epsilon_\delta)+D_\star\epsilon_\delta+2K_u\delta.
\]

After restricting \(\zeta\) to \([0,D_\star]\), the primal feasible set is a nonempty compact polytope. Its Lagrangian uses \(\ell_i\geq0\) for coverage, \(\pi_i\geq0\) for risk, and unrestricted \(\eta_o\) for normalization. Finiteness in \(\zeta\) forces \(\sum_i\pi_i=1\), and finiteness in \(x_{oA}\geq0\) gives
\[
\eta_o\leq c_A\sum_i\pi_ip_{io}-\sum_{i\in A}\ell_ip_{io}.
\]
The dual objective is \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}\sum_i\ell_i+\sum_o\eta_o\). Separating the epigraph of the finite linear image of the compact primal polytope from a point strictly below it supplies these multipliers; weak duality gives the reverse inequality. Thus primal and dual values are equal and feasible points certify the two directions.

Mix a level \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}-\epsilon_h\) rule with the full-set action using probability
\[
\beta=\frac{\epsilon_\delta+\epsilon_h}{\alpha+\epsilon_h}.
\]
This reaches level \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}+\epsilon_\delta\) and adds at most \(D_\star\beta\) cost. The sandwich gap is therefore at most
\[
D_\star\!\left\{\frac{\epsilon_\delta+\epsilon_h}{\alpha+\epsilon_h}+\epsilon_\delta+\epsilon_h\right\}+2K_u\delta,
\]
which vanishes. On bounded boxes, explicit Gaussian density derivative bounds give certified Riemann enclosures; the tail is bounded above. Curve distances have finite primal--dual conic enclosures. Rowwise probability errors perturb coverage and risk by their total-variation errors, while distance errors perturb cost by their uniform error. Sending all enclosures to zero proves the theorem. If \(D_\star=0\), the known singleton curve has value zero directly.

Let \(q=1-\alpha\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:certified\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}value}\) gives, for each \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}>0\), a bounded finite padded-envelope Gaussian rule with coverage \(q\) and worst-case expected loss at most \(L_\alpha+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}/3\). Apply the panel-to-Gaussian kernel, pad for the uniform target error, and mix with the full local envelope to repair vanishing undercoverage. Undoing centering and \(\sqrt n\) scaling gives observed-panel intervals satisfying
\[
\liminf_n\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}P_{\theta_n(u)}\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))\in\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}(v_n(t))\ \forall t\in\mathcal D\}\geq q
\]
and
\[
\limsup_n\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\mathbb E_{\theta_n(u)}
\left[\sup_{t\in\mathcal D}\sqrt n\,\operatorname{diam}\widetilde C_n^{(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}})}(v_n(t))\right]
\leq L_\alpha+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.
\]
Thus the sequence is in the panel honesty class.

Conversely, suppose a panel-honest sequence had, along a subsequence, worst-case scaled expected width at most \(L_\alpha-\epsilon\). Center, scale, and clip its sections to the deterministic local envelope. Coverage is preserved and loss becomes bounded. The reverse kernel followed by target padding gives Gaussian bands with coverage \(q-o(1)\) and risk at most \(L_\alpha-\epsilon+o(1)\). A mixture with the full Gaussian envelope of probability \(o(1)/\{\alpha+o(1)\}\) restores coverage \(q\) at cost \(o(1)\), contradicting the definition of \(L_\alpha\). This proves the lower bound.

Choose \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\) and increasing \(n_k\) such that coverage deficit, transfer error, and excess risk are at most \(\varepsilon_k\) for \(n\geq n_k\). Use rule \(k\) for \(n_k\leq n<n_{k+1}\), with the repair mixture. The diagonal sequence is honest; its limsup loss is at most \(L_\alpha\), and the converse makes its liminf at least \(L_\alpha\). Its primal rules and dual bounds are the certified finite ones. The global projection band \(C_n\) is not used.

If \(\mathcal C_0\) is a linear space, its \(H_0\)-orthogonal projection is linear. Since \(Q(u,t)\) is linear, the critical-cone solution is
\[
h(u,t)=-\Pi_{\mathcal C_0}^{H_0}H_0^{-1}Q(u,t)=H_u u+H_t t.
\]
Because \(a(u)\) is linear, there are vectors \(a_\star,b_\star\) with
\[
\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=a_\star^\prime u+b_\star^\prime t.
\]
Subtracting the known function \(b_\star^\prime t\) from every section preserves widths and coverage and leaves scalar target \(a_\star^\prime u\). Conversely, adding it to any confidence interval for \(a_\star^\prime u\) gives a simultaneous curve band of the same width. The decision values are therefore equal, including value zero when \(a_\star=0\).

At a boundary, the local map is finite piecewise affine and the certified program applies without strict complementarity. No ordering follows from the face label alone. Adding a known function of \(t\) leaves the value unchanged, while replacing \(\Psi\) by \(c\Psi\) multiplies \(L_\alpha\) by \(|c|\). Positive rescaling is realized in the panel model by changing outcome units by \(\sqrt c\) and scaling \(\rho\) by \(c\): weights and face geometry stay fixed, prediction risk and its local curve multiply by \(c\), and standardized Gaussian information is unchanged. The hinge construction supplies a nonzero boundary decision, while an interior point of its two-donor edge supplies a separated affine decision. Equal scaling matches their scalar values; slightly larger or smaller admissible scaling makes either one larger. Thus positive, zero, and negative differences are possible once information and derivatives change, and no compulsory kink surcharge exists.

For \(F_{\mathrm{pre}}(a)=\operatorname{diag}(a,1)\),
\[
A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}0&a&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
a_0(a)=\begin{pmatrix}3a/2\\3/2\end{pmatrix},\quad
d=(0,1,0)^\prime.
\]
The rows of \(A(a)\) are nonzero and orthogonal for \(a>0\), so rank is two. Moreover \(A(a)^+a_0(a)=(0,3/2,3/2)^\prime\), hence \(d^\prime A(a)^+a_0(a)=3/2\) and \(\dot c(u)=0\). At \(a=1\), with predictor weight \((s,1-s)\), the KKT equations give
\[
w=(0,z,1-z),\qquad z=\operatorname{clip}\left\{\frac{40s-9}{22},0,1\right\}.
\]
The excluded donor slack is positive: on the interior edge its equality multiplier is
\[
\eta=-\frac{40}{11}s^2+\frac{40}{11}s+\frac9{220}>0,\qquad 9/40\leq s\leq31/40,
\]
and at both vertices it is at least \(27/40\). Thus this is the full three-donor solution.

Diagonal covariance gives
\[
R(z)=(3/2-z)^2+1+4z^2+(1-z)^2=\frac{17}{4}-5z+6z^2.
\]
Thus \(R'(1)=7\), \(s_0=31/40\), \(w_0=(0,1,0)\), and \(b_0=1/2\). Before clipping,
\[
z_{\mathrm{unc}}(a,s)=\frac{30a^2s+10s-9}{2(10a^2s-10s+11)},\qquad
s_{\mathrm{bdry}}(a)=\frac{31}{10(a^2+3)}.
\]
At \((a,s)=(1,31/40)\),
\[
\partial_a z_{\mathrm{unc}}=\frac{31}{44},\qquad
\partial_s z_{\mathrm{unc}}=\frac{20}{11},\qquad
\partial_a s_{\mathrm{bdry}}=-\frac{31}{80}.
\]
The changed first-block mean derivative is \((3/2,0,1,0)^\prime\). Since \(p_1=1/2\) and \(\Sigma^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1/4,1)\),
\[
I=\frac12(3/2,0,1,0)\Sigma^{-1}(3/2,0,1,0)^\prime
=\frac12\left(\frac94+\frac14\right)=\frac54.
\]
The displayed signals are bounded, and at the center \(A_0\) has two singular values equal to one. Independent Gaussian errors are stationary, geometrically beta-mixing, and sub-Gaussian. Moreover \(\Omega=\operatorname{Var}(\phi_t)\) is block diagonal between its linear and centered-quadratic parts. Its linear block is \(\Sigma\), while for every nonzero symmetric \(B\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_t^\prime B\varepsilon_t)=2\operatorname{tr}\{(\Sigma^{1/2}B\Sigma^{1/2})^2\}>0.
\]
Thus the long-run moment covariance is positive definite and all model conditions hold with fixed finite spectral constants. All other local derivatives vanish. Upper clipping gives
\[
\sqrt n(z_n-1)\longrightarrow\min\left\{\frac{20}{11}t+\frac{31}{44}u,0\right\},
\]
so
\[
\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=7\min\left\{\frac{20}{11}t+\frac{31}{44}u,0\right\}.
\]

Put \(\sigma=\sqrt{4/5}\), \(\kappa=217/44\), and \(\ell=L_0/\sqrt2\). The condition \(m\leq80L_0/(31\sqrt2)\) makes \(t=-\ell\) attain the full separation
\[
D_b=2\kappa m=\frac{217m}{22}
\]
between curves for \(-m,m\). A two-curve envelope has width zero or \(D_b\), according as it reports one or both. Symmetrization under \((u,Z)\mapsto(-u,-Z)\) cannot raise maximum cost or lower minimum coverage. Outside the both-curves action, the sign-selected singleton maximizes Gaussian coverage. The likelihood ratio is monotone, so an exchange from larger to smaller \(|z|\) shows that the cheapest both-curves region is central: \(|Z|\leq h\).

If \(m<\sigma z_{1-\alpha}\), coverage under \(u=m\) requires
\[
1-\alpha=P_m\{Z\geq-h\}=\Phi\!\left(\frac{m+h}{\sigma}\right),\qquad h=\sigma z_{1-\alpha}-m.
\]
Then
\[
P_m\{|Z|\leq h\}=\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha}-\frac{2m}{\sigma}\right)-\alpha.
\]
The same holds at \(-m\). If \(m\geq\sigma z_{1-\alpha}\), sign selection alone has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) and zero width. Therefore the exact binary minimax value is
\[
\frac{217m}{22}\max\left\{\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha}-2m\sqrt{\frac54}\right)-\alpha,0\right\}.
\]
The central-region exchange proves optimality. The maximum's argument is positive exactly when \(z_{1-\alpha}-2m/\sigma>-z_{1-\alpha}\), namely \(m<z_{1-\alpha}/\sqrt{5/4}\). This proves all asserted calculations.

theorem.statement:
There exist parameter-independent Markov kernels from the exact observed Gaussian panel experiment to \(Z\sim N(u,I(\theta_0)^{-1})\) and in the reverse direction such that both deficiencies converge to zero uniformly over \(u\in\mathcal U\). The kernels may be constructed from Gaussian block-mean and residual-scatter sufficient statistics after removing parameter-free ancillary rotations. Moreover,
\[
\sup_{u\in\mathcal U,\ t\in\mathcal D}\left|\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}-\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]
After clipping to the compact family envelope, the kernels transport simultaneous coverage and expected maximum width in both directions; deterministic target padding and vanishing-probability mixing with the full envelope repair target and coverage errors. Thus the compact-local panel and Gaussian-shift band experiments have the same asymptotic minimax bounded curve-diameter value.
theorem.proof_tex:
Index pre group \(\ell\) by dimension \(J+1\), count \(n_\ell\), mean \(m_\ell(\theta)\), and covariance \(\Sigma(\theta)\). Add the post-donor group of dimension \(J\), count \(T_1\), mean \(d(\theta)\), and covariance \(\Sigma_{DD}(\theta)\). Sampling fractions stay positive and covariance eigenvalues stay uniformly bounded away from zero. In local coordinates the directional score of one \(N(\mu_g,\Sigma_g)\) observation is
\[
s_g(y)[u]=D\mu_g[u]^\prime\Sigma_g^{-1}(y-\mu_g)
+\frac12\left\{(y-\mu_g)^\prime\Sigma_g^{-1}D\Sigma_g[u]\Sigma_g^{-1}(y-\mu_g)-\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_g^{-1}D\Sigma_g[u])\right\}.
\]
Let \(\Delta_n\in\mathbb R^q\) be \(n^{-1/2}\) times the coordinate score sum. Gaussian odd moments make mean and covariance scores orthogonal. Direct second-moment evaluation gives \(\operatorname{Var}_0(\Delta_n)\to I(\theta_0)\), exactly the four terms displayed in the definition of \(I(\theta_0)\).

Matrix inversion and \(\log\det\) are smooth on the spectral neighborhood. Taylor expansion at displacement \(u/\sqrt n\), summed over groups, gives uniformly on \(\mathcal U\)
\[
\log\frac{dP_{\theta_n(u)}}{dP_{\theta_0}}
=u^\prime\Delta_n-\frac12u^\prime I(\theta_0)u+r_n(u),\qquad
\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}|r_n(u)|\to_{P_{\theta_0}}0.
\]
Linear and centered-quadratic Gaussian score summands have a common moment generating function near zero. Characteristic-function multiplication and Fourier inversion, splitting into a fixed ball and its complement, give
\[
\mathcal L_{\theta_0}(\Delta_n)\longrightarrow N(0,I(\theta_0))
\]
in total variation. The exponential-moment bound also makes remainders uniformly integrable, so the likelihood-ratio process converges in \(L^1\), uniformly on \(\mathcal U\), to
\[
\Lambda_u(\Delta)=\exp\{u^\prime\Delta-\tfrac12u^\prime I(\theta_0)u\},\qquad \Delta\sim N(0,I(\theta_0)).
\]

For an explicit kernel construction, define an approximate law on the original sample by the center density
\[
\frac{d\widetilde P_{n,u}}{dP_{\theta_0}}
=c_n(u)^{-1}\exp\{u^\prime\Delta_n-\tfrac12u^\prime I(\theta_0)u\},
\qquad
c_n(u)=\mathbb E_{\theta_0}\exp\{u^\prime\Delta_n-\tfrac12u^\prime I(\theta_0)u\}.
\]
Uniform exponential integrability and the likelihood expansion imply
\[
\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}|c_n(u)-1|\to0,\qquad
\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\|\widetilde P_{n,u}-P_{\theta_n(u)}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0.
\]
In the approximate experiment \(\Delta_n\) is sufficient because every likelihood ratio is a function of it. Thus the forward kernel reports \(\Delta_n\), and the reverse kernel draws from the center conditional law of the exact Gaussian sufficient statistic given \(\Delta_n\). The center law of \(\Delta_n\) converges in total variation to \(N(0,I)\); exponential tilting preserves this convergence uniformly for \(u\) in the compact set, so the induced law converges uniformly to \(N(Iu,I)\). The linear transformation \(Z=I^{-1}\Delta\) gives \(N(u,I^{-1})\). Composing the conditional kernel with a common-part total-variation coupling between the score laws yields parameter-independent kernels in both directions. Their deficiencies are bounded by the two displayed total-variation errors and therefore vanish uniformly. Normal group likelihoods depend only on block means and residual scatters; conditional kernels regenerate the center-ancillary residual rotations.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:local\mbox{-}risk\mbox{-}map}\) gives the displayed target error \(\beta_n\to0\). Define
\[
I_n(t)=\left[\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\Psi_n(u,t),\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\Psi_n(u,t)\right],\qquad
\Psi_n(u,t)=\sqrt n\{R_{P_{\theta_n(u)}}(v_n(t))-R_{P_{\theta_0}}(v_0)\}.
\]
Compactness and uniform convergence bound its maximum diameter by \(D<\infty\). Intersect any band with \(I_n(t)\), using a singleton when empty. Every covered curve remains covered and width cannot increase, so loss is bounded. A kernel error \(\kappa_n\) changes coverage and expected loss by at most \(\kappa_n\) and \(D\kappa_n\). Padding by \(\beta_n\) transports targets and adds at most \(2\beta_n\). If coverage is \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}-\gamma_n\), where \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}=1-\alpha\), mixing with the full envelope with probability \(\gamma_n/(\alpha+\gamma_n)\) restores \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}\) and adds at most \(D\gamma_n/(\alpha+\gamma_n)\). All errors vanish, proving bidirectional decision transfer.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For any admissible interval band and any finite parameter set \(F\subset\mathcal U\), let \(A_F\) be the random subset of points in \(F\) whose entire curves are covered. Then \(c(A_F)=\max_{u,u'\in A_F}d_\Psi(u,u')\) is no larger than the band's maximum width, and each grid-point coverage probability is preserved. Conversely, every measurable rule selecting a subset \(A\subseteq F\) induces the pointwise envelope band of those selected curves, with maximum width exactly \(c(A)\), and padding this envelope by the uniform \(u\)-modulus transports coverage from a finite net to \(\mathcal U\). For each pair \((u,u')\), \(d_\Psi(u,u')\) is the maximum of finitely many second-order-cone programs obtained by intersecting the two critical-cone cell systems with \(\mathcal D\). These finite-set reductions apply to every randomized measurable interval-section band and do not impose a nonrandom-shape restriction.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen assertion that the pointwise envelope accepts exactly the same continuum of curves is false: an unaccepted curve can lie pointwise between accepted curves. The finite accepted-set reduction is the true statement needed by the lower bound and applies to every original randomized measurable band.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(q_{\mathrm{cov}}=1-\alpha\), \(D_\star=\sup_{u,u'\in\mathcal U}d_\Psi(u,u')\), and let \(K_u\) satisfy \(\sup_t|\Psi(u,t)-\Psi(u',t)|\leq K_u\|u-u'\|_2\). For a \(\delta\)-net, put \(\epsilon_\delta=\sup_{\|u-u_i\|\leq\delta}\operatorname{TV}\{N(u,I^{-1}),N(u_i,I^{-1})\}\). For the observation partition and a parameter-independent within-cell reconstruction kernel, let \(\epsilon_h\) be its uniform deficiency, including the tail cell. Whenever \(\epsilon_h\leq q_{\mathrm{cov}}\) and \(\epsilon_\delta\leq\alpha\), certified Gaussian probabilities and conic distances give
\[
V_{N,h}(q_{\mathrm{cov}}-\epsilon_h)-D_\star\epsilon_h
\leq L_\alpha(\theta_0,v_0;M,L_0)
\leq V_{N,h}(q_{\mathrm{cov}}+\epsilon_\delta)+D_\star\epsilon_\delta+2K_u\delta.
\]
The primal and dual programs have the same finite value and respectively certify feasible upper and lower bounds. One may take \(\epsilon_\delta\leq\|I^{1/2}\|\delta/\sqrt{2\pi}\) and an explicit \(\epsilon_h\to0\) whenever \(R\to\infty\), \(h\to0\), and hence under \(hR\to0\). If \(\delta\to0\), \(R\to\infty\), \(hR\to0\), and numerical enclosure errors vanish, the certified gap converges to zero. The padded envelope rules are asymptotically minimax among all externally randomized measurable interval-section bands.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: For a coarse mesh, the frozen universal quantifier can request \(V_{N,h}\) outside its domain because \(q+\epsilon_\delta>1\) or \(q-\epsilon_h<0\). The corrected claim states the computable sandwich under the necessary level conditions and retains the full convergent characterization.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: \(C_n(v)=[\inf_{\theta\in E_n}R_{P_\theta}(v),\sup_{\theta\in E_n}R_{P_\theta}(v)]\) when \(E_n\neq\varnothing\); if \(E_n=\varnothing\), return the zero-diameter interval \([0,0]\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Returning \(\mathbb R\) when \(E_n\) is empty gives infinite diameter on an event that need not have vanishing probability, contradicting the claimed root-\(n\) stochastic diameter bound. A fixed singleton preserves the coverage proof on \(\{\theta_P\in E_n\}\) and has zero diameter.

proposed.statement: Under the single criterion \(L_\alpha\), if the critical cone \(\mathcal C_0\) is a linear space, then \(\Psi_{\theta_0}(u,t)=a_{\star}^{\prime}u+b_{\star}^{\prime}t\) and the risk-graph decision reduces exactly to scalar Gaussian confidence-interval inference for \(a_{\star}^{\prime}u\). At a boundary face the same certified program applies, and the difference from a separated face may be positive, zero, or negative after the information and derivatives change; no compulsory positive kink penalty is asserted.
